discovery: The optical lattice clock: invention and realization of atomic clocks with 10^-18 precision using neutral atoms in magic-wavelength optical lattices

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics; precision measurement
motivation: Katori proposed (2001-2003) and first demonstrated trapping many neutral atoms in an optical lattice at a 'magic' wavelength, where the light shifts of both clock states cancel. This removes the perturbation from confinement while keeping the stability gained from interrogating thousands of atoms at once. Jun Ye turned the concept into the most accurate and stable clocks ever built, reaching systematic uncertainties near 10^-18 through deep control of atomic interactions, laser stabilization and frequency combs. Lattice clocks now resolve the gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, set stringent limits on variation of fundamental constants and on dark matter, enable relativistic geodesy, and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. This is exemplary atomic physics: painstaking laboratory precision that opens new windows on fundamental questions far beyond its own field.
